overview: The sub-summit is reached from the notch between the two high points. The climbing itself is 5.2, yet getting back out of the notch takes a 5.6 dihedral. overview: Five pitches of jams and corners in fine stone, ending where it meets the last pair of pitches on Leisure Climb. The hardest technical moves come in the thin crack of pitch two.

approach: From Grand Lake, take West Portal Road out to the East Inlet trailhead; the East Inlet trail runs on to the far end of Lake Verna. From the far end of the lake, go a short way toward Spirit Lake, then take the easiest line south across the creek and up steep forest to the foot of Aiguille de Fleur.

name: Atalanta
overview: A short, easy line near the left margin of the First Flatiron's slab that shares its start with Hubris, then carries on up a groove past a juniper to a decent ledge.

descent: two 100 ft raps from the 2-bolt anchor atop pitch 4, or go on to the summit
name: Athlete's Feat
overview: A historic Boulder Canyon route whose third pitch, an overhanging crack, was freed in the 1960s and counted among the earliest hard 5.10 leads anywhere.

name: Backflip
overview: A popular 5.9 on the south side: a right-facing flake and corner to a flat ledge, then a big dihedral where you either undercling right to the ridge or pull the roof straight to the top.

descent: rap 100 ft west from the summit eyebolt
name: Baker's Way
overview: A gentle First Flatiron outing: once past a steep first wall up to two small pines, a long ramp slants right and north for several pitches until it meets the North Arete.

approach: Park in the pulloff just past the eighteenth highway marker, by the interpretive sheep sign. descent: The climbing ends on the summit plateau, and the car is a short walk back along the road across the rocks. Step on rock rather than on the fragile alpine plants.

overview: Decent protection, some choss, and little route finding; keep to the arete. Take care not to knock rocks down onto the belayer or other parties. name: Anus Grape
overview: Direct variation on the third pitch of the Wild Side route. Starting at the belay that tops its second pitch, climb over the roof by way of the big block wedged out of the lip, then work up a strenuous offwidth for probably 50-60 feet. name: Solar Winds
overview: P1: the opening pitch of the Wild Side route (5.10c/d), up to its hanging belay. name: Miller's Face

name: Blinded
overview: An easy 200 ft east-facing climb on the little crag closest to where The Thing starts, in Bluebell Canyon; getting off means jumping a gap at the top.

overview: The vertical chimney that cuts the buttress into upper and lower halves, which a horizontal ledge divides again into four blocks.

name: Crack of Fear
overview: Colorado's best-known offwidth: about 250 ft of crack that stays 5 inches or wider up the East Owl, strenuous and relentless from the Rat's Tooth to the final ramp.

name: Curtains
overview: A route on Window Rock, the slender pierced spine near the park's Fall River gate.

name: Dark Obsession
overview: A poorly protected face line on the Achean Pronouncement that starts with a layback and joins the crest to the top.

name: Direct Route
overview: The classic full-length First Flatiron line: about ten pitches from the lowest tip of the slab, a run-out first pitch, a steep headwall on big holds, a chimney slot, then the upper North Arete.

name: East Face Left
overview: The longest outing on the Third Flatiron: a rib, ramps beside the big overhang, then many pitches along the left margin to where the Gash ends, joining the regular finish. Gear is thin.

name: East Face (Standard)
overview: Boulder's classic beginner climb: about 800 ft of easy, sparsely protected slab up the Third Flatiron linked by big old eyebolts, finishing beside the Gash.

name: Safari Land
overview: Begins on the Trunk Line start, then steps right over the roof to reach a bolt.

overview: Starts in the giant Eumenides corner, then spends most of its five pitches on the slab west of it before finishing up a higher left-facing corner with a roof that goes either side at 5.8.

descent: rap 100 ft west from the summit eyebolts, then follow the switchbacking trail south of the rock
name: Fandango
overview: A popular alternative to Direct East Face: slab climbing that skirts a roof by keeping left, a short corner and small roofs, then a long left-facing corner that tops out on the North Arete below its quartz-crystal step.
